name: Strandfontein (West Coast)
coord_source: Wannasurf 'Strandfontein beachbreak' spot page prints 31°45.019'S 18°13.453'E (-31.7503,18.2242); Surfline's 'Curlew Strand' anchor (-31.7542,18.2263) is 450 m south on the same beach and Nominatim's Strandfontein village is -31.7556,18.2272
best_season: summer (Nov to Mar) small to medium NW-W swells per Wannasurf; calm or berg-wind mornings in any season
description: A fun but fickle right-hand beach break at the holiday village north of Doringbaai, best in a small to medium swell on an incoming tide with no wind or a hot berg wind. The sandbanks move around a lot in rippy conditions.
local_notes: Wannasurf: beach break, right, sandy with rock, hollow/powerful/fun, NW swell, S wind, 'starts working at less than 1 m and holds up to 2 m+', all tides on the push and drop, very consistent (150 days/yr), short rides, 'gets very good especially in summer', empty, all surfers, 'cold but lekker', rips and sharks, 'best in calm or berg winds during a small to medium swell and incoming tide'. The beach faces WNW, so E-ESE (berg) winds are the true offshore and a S wind is side-shore; the wider tolerance covers both. Surfline's 'Curlew Strand' is the same beach under another name. Size basis: shows from under 1 m offshore and closes out beyond about 2.5 m. Not the False Bay Strandfontein.
sources: Surfline anchor list supplied in the task brief (Curlew Strand)
bottom: beach break (fickle right-handers over shifting sand with rock)

name: Doring Bay
coord_source: Wannasurf 'Doring Bay' spot page prints 31°48.983'S 18°13.97'E (-31.8164,18.2328); Nominatim 'Doringbaai' natural=bay (-31.8139,18.2364) agrees within 450 m
best_season: winter (May to Aug) for a clean 4-6 ft NW groundswell with SE or E winds
description: A hollow, powerful left over reef in a small fishing-harbour bay north of Lambert's Bay, with rides of 50 to 150 m normally and up to 300 to 500 m on a clean NW groundswell. Freezing cold, a long drive, and a regional classic.
local_notes: Wannasurf: left reef break, reef bottom, hollow/powerful, NW swell, SE/E wind, 'starts working at 1.0-1.5 m and holds up to 3 m+', best in a 'clean 4-6 ft groundswell', all tides, rising and falling, regular consistency, regional classic, empty to few surfers, all surfers, rocks and localism, 'freezing cold here but you won't care when you see the wave'. The bay faces NW, so SW groundswell wraps in smaller (semi) and NW swell arrives direct. Size basis: 1.5 m offshore at 14 s to break properly; around 4 m the reef maxes out. Wannasurf rates it 'all surfers' but a hollow reef left with rocks and localism is an intermediate wave at least.
bottom: left-hand reef break (point-like on its day)

name: Lambert's Bay
coord_source: Wannasurf 'Lamberts Bay' spot page prints 32°5.04'S 18°18.759'E (-32.0840,18.3127); Nominatim's Lambert's Bay caravan park (-32.0866,18.3134) is 300 m away
crowd: light; a few locals most days
best_season: year-round (very consistent); winter (May to Aug) NW-W swell wrapping past Bird Island with light S-SE winds
description: A friendly rights-and-lefts wave in front of the caravan park and river mouth, tucked behind Bird Island and the harbour so the swell wraps in with its teeth pulled. Easy, consistent and best in light wind with a moderate swell.
local_notes: Wannasurf: beach break, rights and lefts, sandy with rock, hollow to ordinary, NW and W swell, S wind, 'starts working at less than 1 m and holds up to 3 m+', low and mid tide, very consistent (150 days/yr), few surfers, all surfers, localism, 'near the caravan park at the rivermouth', 'easy wave, best in light wind and moderate swell'. Wesgro's Weskus guide names it 'Yo-yos, a reef break in front of the caravan park that goes both left and right'; surf-forecast.com lists 'Caravan Park/Lamberts Bay' 26 km from Elands Bay. The beach sits inside the bay behind the island and harbour wall and faces north-west, which is why S-SE winds are offshore and NW-W swell is best; SW swell has to wrap and arrives much smaller (semi). Size basis: works from about 1.2 m offshore and holds to 4 m thanks to the wrap. Beginner-friendly on size, but the locals expect manners.
sources: https://www.surf-forecast.com/breaks/The-Point_3 (names 'Caravan Park/Lamberts Bay' as a nearby break)
bottom: beach break over sand and rock in front of the caravan park at the river mouth (a reef peak locals call Yo-Yos)

name: Elands Bay
coord_source: Surfline anchor 'Elands Bay' (-32.3142,18.3311); surf-forecast.com prints 32.31S 18.32E for 'The Point (Elands Bay)'
crowd: heavy when it is on (weekends, holidays, every forecast swell); moderate otherwise
best_season: autumn and winter (Apr to Aug): SW groundswell behind cold fronts with S-SE winds; surf-forecast.com rates April the most consistent clean month
description: The West Coast's jewel: a long, reeling, kelpy left point under Baboon Point with a hollow take-off and a fast cylindrical wall that runs 150 m or more toward the river mouth. Cold, windy, crowded when it fires, and worth every one of the 220 km from Cape Town.
local_notes: Three sources agree: surf-forecast.com (reef, point and river mouth; SW swell ideal; SE offshore; rocks and kelp; 'sometimes crowded'; winter optimum, April 65% clean; ability 4/10), Zigzag's spot check (prefers SW swell but also responds to northerly swell; offshore in southerly winds; 'pushing tide is great', morning spring lows and afternoon spring highs best, low tide excellent on glassy days; too much swell makes the longshore sweep 'completely overpowering'; time the paddle-out to miss the dry rock shelves; intermediate to advanced; kites and windsurfers at full speed are the main hazard) and the sani.co.za guide (world-class left point, SE winds, NW swell, experienced surfers). Wannasurf's index rates it high consistency, experienced surfers; Wesgro calls it 'arguably the best surf spot in the Western Cape'. The point faces NW, so SW swell wraps around Baboon Point and arrives smaller than offshore (hence semi) while W-NW storm swell comes straight in. Size basis: needs about 1.5 m offshore at 14 s to run; holds well past 4 m but by 5 m offshore the sweep and the paddle become the problem. Nearby per surf-forecast.com: Baboon Point and Guyztus Point (2 km), Farmer Burgers (15 km), Garbage Dump (24 km), not placed.
sources: Surfline anchor list supplied in the task brief (Elands Bay)
bottom: left-hand point break over a kelp-covered rock shelf, running onto sand toward the river mouth

name: Trekoskraal
coord_source: Wannasurf 'Groot Trekoskraal' spot page prints 32°54.652'S 17°51.9'E (-32.9109,17.8650); Nominatim's Trekoskraal camp site (-32.8870,17.8736) is 2.8 km north on the same coast
best_season: winter (May to Aug) on a long-period SW groundswell with light east or berg winds
description: A camping and crayfish-diving coast between Jacobsbaai and Paternoster where a small right-hander rolls into a deep bay. It needs a specific deep groundswell and light easterly winds, so it is fickle, but it surprises you when it is on.
local_notes: Wannasurf 'Groot Trekoskraal': reef-rocky, right, sandy with rock, ordinary power, short rides (50-150 m on good days), 'starts working at 1.0-1.5 m and holds up to 2.5 m+', mid tide, both rising and falling, regular but 'not very consistent, good when it's on', winter, empty, all surfers, 'requires specific deep groundswell conditions' and 'light east/berg winds'. Its wind field lists NW as good and E/berg as acceptable: NW is side-shore on this WSW-facing coast, so E is recorded as offshore with the NW note kept here. Size basis: a wrapping right that needs about 2 m offshore at 14 s+ to show and holds to about 4.5 m. Wannasurf also lists 'Klein Trekoskraal' (rights and lefts, beach break, 3/5 consistency), not opened.
bottom: right-hand reef wrapping into a small deep bay (Groot); beach-break peaks at Klein Trekoskraal

name: Jacobsbaai
coord_source: Nominatim 'Jacobsbaai' natural=bay (-32.9650,17.8864); no surf source printed a coordinate
best_season: winter (May to Aug) for SW groundswell; calm or easterly (berg-wind) mornings
description: A quiet fishing village north of Saldanha with a string of small rocky bays (Smalbaai, Kwaaibaai and neighbours) that offer reef and beach peaks on a SW swell, well off the main surf trail.
local_notes: Named as 'Jacobs Bay' (rating 4.0) on surf-forecast.com's Yzerfontein nearby-break list, but no spot page was opened, so the parameters are geographic: W-SW-facing rocky coast, E offshore, sizes 1 m to about 3 m offshore as for the Trekoskraal and Paternoster coast. Tide unverified. Several Wannasurf West Coast reefs with nicknames (Baby Pipes, Boneyard CJ, Rollers, Stovepipes, Suicide Reef and others) probably sit on this stretch but could not be placed.
bottom: reef and beach breaks in a series of small rocky bays

name: West Coast National Park (Tsaarsbank)
coord_source: Surfline anchor 'West Coast National Park' (-33.1894,18.0571), on the Atlantic shore of the park's Postberg peninsula; Nominatim returned nothing for Tsaarsbank
best_season: winter (May to Aug) for W-SW groundswell; park gate hours apply (later opening in winter)
description: The Atlantic beaches inside the West Coast National Park, reached through the Langebaan gate: wild, uncrowded sandbar peaks between rock outcrops with the park entry fee as the only crowd control.
local_notes: Named only by Surfline (as 'West Coast National Park') among the sources opened; no surf guide with parameters was reached, so the window, wind and sizes are geographic: WSW-facing open coast, ENE offshore, closes out beyond about 3 m offshore. Treat as a low-confidence placeholder until a spot page is opened. Tsaarsbank is on the public part of the park road; the Postberg section beyond it opens only in flower season (Aug to Sep).
sources: Surfline anchor list supplied in the task brief (West Coast National Park)
bottom: beach break with rock outcrops

name: Yzerfontein Main Beach
coord_source: Wannasurf '16 MILE BEACH' spot page (alternative name 'Yzerfontein Main Beach') prints 33°21.541'S 18°9.28'E (-33.3590,18.1547), 1 km south of the harbour on the main beach; surf-forecast.com prints 33.33S 18.16E
crowd: light on weekdays; crowded when it is working
best_season: winter (May to Aug) for WSW groundswell (surf-forecast.com rates June the most consistent); it works year-round
description: The town beach south of Yzerfontein harbour: sandbar peaks on the beach and lefts and rights off the reefs just outside, 45 minutes from Cape Town and still quieter than the city beaches.
local_notes: surf-forecast.com 'Yzerfontein': exposed beach and reef break, lefts and rights on both the beach and the offshore reefs, best swell WSW, offshore E, 'watch out for rocks', winter/June best, ability 4/10, 'can get crowded'. Wannasurf's page (titled '16 MILE BEACH', alt name 'Yzerfontein Main Beach'): left beach break, sandy with rock, fun, regular consistency, regional classic, empty to few surfers, all surfers, car park a minute from the water, 'still undiscovered'; its swell, wind and tide fields are blank, so the mid tide here is unverified. Size basis: beach peaks from 1 m offshore; the reefs hold up to about 3.5 m. The long beach running south from here is the separate '16 Mile Beach' entry. Yzerfontein is also a wave-sailing and kite spot in the summer south-easter.
bottom: beach break with offshore reef peaks (lefts and rights)

name: 16 Mile Beach
area: south of Yzerfontein toward the West Coast National Park
coord_source: Surfline anchor 'Yzerfontein' (-33.372,18.152), which falls on 16 Mile Beach about 2.5 km south of the harbour
crowd: light; walk and you will have a peak to yourself
best_season: winter (May to Aug) for WSW groundswell; small clean summer mornings before the south-easter
description: South Africa's longest uninterrupted beach, running 16 miles from Yzerfontein to the national park: endless unnamed sandbar peaks that favour a clean, smaller swell because the open banks close out fast when it is big.
local_notes: Wannasurf lists '16 MILE BEACH' (left beach break, regular consistency) and surf-forecast.com's Yzerfontein page covers the same stretch (WSW swell, E offshore, rocks at the town end), so the parameters are inherited from the Yzerfontein entry with an earlier close-out ceiling: size basis 0.8 m to about 2.5 m offshore. Tide unverified. Rips get stronger the further south you walk.
sources: Surfline anchor list supplied in the task brief (Yzerfontein)

area: Grotto Bay, between Silwerstroom and Yzerfontein
coord_source: mondo.surf spot guide prints -33.50031667, 18.3125; Nominatim's Grotto Bay beach parking (-33.5074,18.3145) is 800 m south on the same beach
best_season: winter (May to Aug) for hollow W groundswell; early mornings
description: A private coastal village with a short, punchy beach break: solid, hollow, shorey-style lefts and rights over sand and rock when a groundswell hits, best early on a rising tide.
local_notes: mondo.surf: beach break, sand and rocks, left and right, rides under 50 m, best swell W (247.5-292.5), best wind E-SE (67.5-157.5), medium to high tide on the push, very consistent (150+ days/yr), hollow especially in winter, all levels, empty, 'private property, so access may be limited'. Size basis: a shorebreak that is fun from 1 m offshore and closes out past about 2.5 m. Access is through the village gate, so ask before you drive in.
bottom: beach break (sand and rock; short, hollow shorebreak peaks)

coord_source: Surfline anchor 'Silverstroomstrand' (-33.5813,18.3568); surf-forecast.com prints only 33.47S 18.30E, which is too coarse to use
crowd: light; rarely crowded even when it works
best_season: winter (May to Aug) for WSW groundswell (surf-forecast.com rates June the most consistent); it works year-round

sources: Surfline anchor list supplied in the task brief (Silverstroomstrand)

coord_source: Surfline anchor 'Van Riebeeckstrand' (-33.7,18.4333)

best_season: winter (May to Aug) for W-SW groundswell; glassy or light-easterly mornings

sources: Surfline anchor list supplied in the task brief (Van Riebeeckstrand)

name: Melkbos
coord_source: Surfline anchor 'Melkbosstrand' (-33.719,18.439)
crowd: moderate; heavy at Beach Road on a good winter swell
best_season: winter (May to Aug) for big SW groundswell on the outer reef and the Beach Road right; light SE or glassy mornings
description: Melkbos's long beach has sandbar peaks its whole length, but the spot surfers mean is Beach Road at the south end: a right-hand sandbar point sheltered by an outer reef that takes the brunt of a big groundswell and leaves a long, rideable wall inside.

Tide is unverified; mid is the generic beach-break call.
sources: Surfline anchor list supplied in the task brief (Melkbosstrand)
WebSearch result snippet describing 'Melkbos / Beach Road' (source page not opened)

name: Haakgat
coord_source: Wannasurf 'Haakgat Point' spot page prints 33°45.055'S 18°26.526'E (-33.7509,18.4421); Nominatim 'Haakgat' natural=bay (-33.7519,18.4408) agrees within 150 m
crowd: light; busy with kites and wave-sailors on windy afternoons
best_season: winter (May to Aug) SW groundswell on a rising high tide; summer afternoons are kite territory
description: A sectiony, ledgy left point that peels over reef and sand into a small cove between the steens and Melkbos. Hollow and fast when a SW swell meets a high tide, and better known to the kitesurfing crowd than to surfers.
local_notes: Wannasurf: point break, left, reef with sand, hollow/fast/powerful/ledgy, SW swell, SE/E/NE wind, 'starts at less than 1 m, holds up to 2.5 m+', high tide only on a rising tide, very consistent (150 days/yr), few surfers, experienced surfers, rips and rocks, 'sectiony left point and beach breaks' that can be inconsistent depending on the sandbanks. Size basis: the reef needs about 1.2 m offshore at 12 s+ to run and gets unmanageable past 3.5 m. Haakgat is one of Cape Town's premier wave-kiting spots, so afternoon line-ups are shared.
bottom: left-hand point break over reef and sand, with beach-break peaks alongside

name: Derdesteen
coord_source: Wannasurf '3de Steen' spot page prints 33°46.366'S 18°26.66'E (-33.7728,18.4443); Nominatim returned nothing for Derdesteen. The resort picnic site is within about 1 km north along the same beach.
best_season: winter (May to Aug) for W-SW groundswell; glassy or light-easterly mornings any season
description: The best known of the 'steens' (Eerste, Tweede, Derde Steen) along the coast road north of Big Bay: a powerful, shifty beach break that throws chunky shorebreak barrels when the banks line up in a winter swell.
local_notes: Wannasurf: beach break, rights and lefts, sandy with rock, hollow/fast/powerful, W-SW swell, best at low and mid tide, 'starts working at 1.0-1.5 m and holds up to 2 m+', regular consistency, few surfers on weekdays and crowded at weekends, rocks, 'best in winter swell'. Wannasurf's wind field says N/NE: NE is cross-offshore here, but the beach faces WSW, so E is the true offshore and that is what is recorded. Fully exposed (north of Robben Island's shadow), so it is usually bigger than Big Bay. Size basis: a shorebreak-style beach break that works from 1 m offshore and closes out beyond about 3 m. surf-forecast.com's Big Bay page lists 'Eerste Steen' as a separate beach break 3 km north of Big Bay; Wannasurf also lists '1ste Steen' and '2de Steen' as rights-and-lefts beach breaks (not opened).
bottom: beach break (sand with rock; hollow shorebreak-style peaks)

name: Bloubergstrand
aka: Little Bay (the cove at the village)
coord_source: Surfline anchor 'Bloubergstrand' (-33.794,18.4559). It sits 200 m from the Big Bay anchor; the village beach peaks and the Little Bay cove are 0.5 to 1.5 km south along the shore.
crowd: moderate; heavy with kites in the summer south-easter
best_season: winter (May to Aug) for SW groundswell; summer mornings before the south-easter (Nov to Mar is kite season)
description: The beach in front of Bloubergstrand village, just south of Big Bay, with peaks breaking between granite boulders and a smaller, more sheltered cove at Little Bay. The same swell and wind as Big Bay with a rockier line-up.
local_notes: Wannasurf's Cape Town index lists both 'Blaauwberg' (rights and lefts, beach break, experienced surfers) and 'Little Bay' (rights and lefts, beach break, all surfers); surf-forecast.com's Big Bay page lists 'Blouberg' and 'Little Bay' as beach breaks 2 km away. No spot page was opened, so swell, wind, tide and size follow Big Bay: SW swell, ESE offshore. Partially shadowed from due-W swell by Robben Island, like Big Bay. Size basis as Big Bay with an earlier close-out on the open sand. The sani.co.za guide covers Blouberg as a kitesurf beach with S, SSE and SE winds from November to March. Little Bay was folded in here rather than listed separately because no verified coordinate for the cove was obtained.
sources: Surfline anchor list supplied in the task brief (Bloubergstrand)
bottom: beach break between granite boulders (plus the small Little Bay cove)

name: Big Bay
coord_source: Surfline anchor 'Big Bay' (-33.7954,18.454); Wannasurf prints 33°47.536'S 18°27.064'E (-33.7923,18.4511) and surf-forecast.com 33.79S 18.46E, all within 450 m
crowd: heavy; weekends, summer evenings and any clean day, with surf schools in the shorebreak
best_season: year-round: winter (May to Aug) for size, summer (Nov to Mar) for the cleanest small days with the south-easter offshore (surf-forecast.com rates March the most consistent)
description: The West Coast's everyman beach break, between Bloubergstrand and Melkbos, with a cafe strip and big car park on the sand. Peaky lefts and rights, rights more common, from knee-high to overhead, and it copes with messy conditions better than most.
local_notes: Two sources agree on the key parameters: surf-forecast.com gives SW swell, ESE offshore, good at all stages of tide, rips and rocks, 'often crowded', ability 3/10; Wannasurf gives SE/E wind, all tides, 'starts working at less than 1 m and holds up to 4 m+', rips and rocks, powerful, regional classic. Wannasurf's swell entry of 'East, NorthEast' is a data-entry error for an Atlantic-facing beach and was discarded. Robben Island sits due west and shades straight-W swell, so Big Bay runs smaller than Melkbos or Derdesteen on the same day; SW and NW swell get in cleanly. Size basis: shows on 1.5 m offshore at 12 s+; above about 4.5 m offshore the banks close out and only the outer peaks hold. Beginners stay inside on small days; the outer banks on a big winter swell are intermediate territory.
sources: Surfline anchor list supplied in the task brief (Big Bay)
bottom: beach break (lefts and rights over sand, boulders at each end)

name: Table View
coord_source: Nominatim 'Dolphin Beach Hotel, Marine Drive' (-33.8298,18.4816) shifted about 150 m west onto the beach centre; no surf source printed a coordinate
crowd: moderate; heavy kite traffic at Dolphin Beach in the summer south-easter
best_season: winter (May to Aug) for size; summer mornings before the south-easter fills in (afternoons belong to the kiters)
description: Long, open sandbar beach break along Table View's Marine Drive, launched from the Dolphin Beach car park. Mellow peaks in small to medium swell and the first beach north of the city with real space.
local_notes: Named by Wannasurf's Cape Town index as 'Tableview' (right and left sandbar, all surfers); no spot page opened, so parameters are geographic: the same Table Bay window as Milnerton, slightly more open to W-NW as the bay widens. Size basis as Milnerton. Dolphin Beach is Cape Town's main kitesurf launch; keep clear of the kite zone when the wind is up.
sources: Nominatim (nominatim.openstreetmap.org) query 'Dolphin Beach, Table View, Cape Town'

sources: Nominatim (nominatim.openstreetmap.org) query 'Sunset Beach, Milnerton, Cape Town'

name: Milnerton
coord_source: Surfline anchor 'Milnerton Beach' (-33.8812,18.4868); Wannasurf prints 33°52.873'S 18°29.159'E (-33.8812,18.4860), 70 m apart
crowd: moderate; heavy at weekends and on clean winter mornings
best_season: winter (May to Aug) for W-SW groundswell; works year-round, and the summer south-easter blows offshore so early summer mornings are often clean

sources: Surfline anchor list supplied in the task brief (Milnerton Beach)

name: Off the Wall
coord_source: mondo.surf spot guide prints -33.89833, 18.40408 (Beach Road sea wall near the Mouille Point lighthouse); surf-forecast.com gives only 33.91S 18.39E at 2 dp. Not a Surfline spot.
crowd: moderate - a small keen city crew; crowded when it is on
best_season: winter (May to Sep) W-NW groundswell; summer is mostly flat, but the SE wind is offshore so any summer swell is worth a look
description: Cape Town's inner-city reef: a short, hollow, powerful wave breaking off the Mouille Point sea wall in front of the apartment blocks. Short, sharp take-off and a steep drop over rock.
local_notes: Needs a solid swell to wrap around Green Point into Table Bay, hence the 1.8 m floor and the W-leaning window; above about 4.5 m the inside gets ugly and the wall becomes the hazard. Rising low-to-mid tide (mondo.surf). The SE wind is clean offshore here, which is why surf-forecast.com's statistics favour late summer (72 percent clean in February) while noting summer is mostly flat. Lefts and rights per both sources; capetownmagazine calls it an advanced wave with a short sharp take-off. Thermopylae (Milnerton, outside this region) across the bay is the usual alternative on the same swell.
bottom: reef (rock), left and right, breaking off the promenade sea wall

name: Rocklands
coord_source: Nominatim 'Rocklands Beach, Sea Point' -33.90867, 18.39343. surf-forecast.com prints 33.91S 18.38E and calls it 0 km from Queens, which would put it 1.9 km further south-west; the beach of that name is at the Three Anchor Bay end, so the Nominatim point is used. Verify on the ground.
crowd: moderate - a fairly popular wave that can get crowded when on
best_season: late summer to autumn (Feb to Apr) when SW swell meets the SE wind; winter W swells also work

Low to mid tide; too deep on the sandbar at high. Offshore in anything from SE through S to SW. Surf schools and groms at the south end; the shorebreak gets serious on big days. Surfline's spot guide for this spot returned HTTP 403 on two attempts, so Surfline contributes only the coordinate.
